claim: .claude/rules is supported from v1.0.89.
limitations: Check attachment, scope and precedence with /instructions for your target path.

claim: Command preToolUse nonzero exits deny; dispatcher timeouts fail open.
limitations: Keep independent CI; a timeout is not a deny.

claim: Selective tools are documented, but noninteractive help requires allow-all-tools.
limitations: If narrow grants fail, use manual approvals or stop; do not widen permissions.

claim: AI-credit CLI limits are public-preview soft limits; the dedicated guide says interactive session-wide, the command reference says per-response reset.
limitations: Captured 1.0.89 config help says session scope; lead's 2026-10-02 1.0.90 help-only observation agrees, not a captured artifact or runtime test. In-progress response may exceed limit; check installed help and /usage.

claim: Agent Plugins 1.0 packages a root plugin.json and skill directories.
limitations: Review package contents and installed CLI options before installation.

claim: The local generator makes a deterministic skill-only ZIP validated against the manifest schema.
limitations: Archive validation does not install a plugin.

claim: The synthetic MCP server implements initialize, ping, tools/list and tools/call.
limitations: Protocol tests do not establish Copilot CLI client compatibility.

claim: HydraFusion research preview selects Single, Cascade or Critique and aggregates model and stage usage.
limitations: Vendor-controlled offline benchmark results are not a local savings guarantee; check /model eligibility and /usage; final answer does not show internal route.

claim: Copilot login uses OAuth and separate entitlement, not GitLab credentials.
limitations: Requires an entitled account; GitLab credentials are separate.

claim: Token precedence is COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, then GITHUB_TOKEN; classic ghp_ PATs are unsupported.
limitations: Use a supported token with Copilot Requests permission and entitlement.

claim: Copilot combines applicable CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md and GitHub instruction locations and deduplicates some identical copies.
limitations: Near-duplicates and conflicts remain; no general precedence order. Inspect /instructions for actual attachment.

claim: Repository-relative @ imports are eagerly read in supported instruction files; not expanded in GEMINI.md or path instructions.
limitations: Use repository-relative imports only in supported instruction files; plain references need not load immediately.

claim: Only named shared Claude settings keys have documented Copilot meanings.
limitations: Audit each key; do not copy private credentials.

claim: Subagents have separate contexts; custom subagents need include-custom-instructions true to receive repository instructions.
limitations: Check effective instructions, tools and model on the selected subagent; do not assume full conversation inheritance.

claim: Copilot offers /fleet, /tasks and /rubber-duck.
limitations: Inspect assigned roles and tool permissions before parallel work.

claim: /plan and mode cycling help plan work, but are not OS read-only controls.
limitations: Review plan.md and permissions before implementation.

claim: stayInAutopilot defaults to true after a completed task in captured config help.
limitations: Inspect current mode and /settings after task completion.

claim: Tool visibility, invocation approvals, paths and URL grants are distinct; deny takes precedence.
limitations: Permission filters do not isolate the OS.

claim: --allow-all grants tools, paths and URLs; COPILOT_ALLOW_ALL=true also trusts the working directory.
limitations: Only use in approved disposable isolation; do not set globally.

claim: /model auto routes by task and availability among plan/policy-eligible models, considers cache boundaries, and has profiles; a paid supported-surface 10% model-cost discount is documented.
limitations: Not a guarantee of cheapest or best result; inspect model and /usage; captured help remains the historical 1.0.89 baseline.

claim: Copilot offers continue, resume, fork, worktree, compact and rewind controls.
limitations: Check cwd and current files after resume; rewind does not undo external effects.

claim: --no-remote disables remote control; --no-remote-export disables export and control.
limitations: These flags do not disable model traffic.

claim: --output-format json emits JSONL, not Claude JSON.
limitations: Validate event handling and stdin behavior before automating completion.

claim: The local wrapper checks bounded JSONL framing and returns validation-pending or report-unverified.
limitations: Review the diff and run project checks separately; JSONL framing is not task success.

claim: The local GitLab bridge plans explicit-host GET requests, checks job identity and stores sanitized observations.
limitations: Real reads require reviewed host, IDs and authorization.

claim: glab mr create --fill pushes; explicit source, target and draft flags are available.
limitations: Approve push and MR creation separately; check host and target.

claim: GitLab MCP HTTP access is beta with instance/group enablement.
limitations: Check eligibility and CLI client support before configuring.

claim: /delegate is GitHub cloud delegation, separate from a local GitLab MR.
limitations: Requires a GitHub-hosted target and approval for remote effects.

claim: gh agent-task create/list/view is a GitHub-hosted public preview.
limitations: Check installed gh help and account availability before use.

claim: Agent Plugins schemas/software use Apache 2.0 and specification/docs use CC BY 4.0.
limitations: Recheck attribution requirements if redistributing a changed schema version.

claim: GitHub cloud-agent setup uses .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml with a copilot-setup-steps job on the default branch.
limitations: Requires a GitHub-hosted target and workflow installed on the default branch.

claim: COPILOT_TASK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS controls -p background wait; default is 600 seconds and 0 means no wait.
limitations: Check support in your installed version before relying on the setting.

claim: Usage-based AI credits ($0.01 each) reflect model-priced input, output and cached tokens, some cache writes and long-context tiers; legacy annual request multipliers are separate.
limitations: Do not double-count reasoning already included in reported usage; no universal flat fee per tool call. Context occupancy is not a billing formula; pricing changes. Not runtime verified.

claim: /context reports occupancy including tool definitions/results; large tool output gets temporary-file preview and /compact is lossy model work.
limitations: Default output threshold is above 20 KiB; previews can still lead to later reads. No refund for compaction.

claim: Model changes, inactivity, effort/context/tool changes can invalidate cache; cached input is not universally free.
limitations: Resume does not promise warm cache; compare completed tasks rather than single requests.

claim: Autopilot concepts says five default continuations; command reference says unlimited.
limitations: Captured 1.0.89 and lead's 2026-10-02 1.0.90 help-only observation say five; no authenticated default test or new capture. Specify --max-autopilot-continues; count is messages, not credits or tools.

claim: Fleet workers have separate contexts and can independently consume model interactions; no fixed multiplier applies.
limitations: Actual scheduling/models depend on task, profile and availability; check grants and results.

claim: CLI tool search may defer external tools on supported models with enough tools, while built-ins and configured/named exceptions load eagerly.
limitations: Roughly 30 tool threshold and lookup overhead; inspect /context and actual server contract, do not invent filter parameters.

claim: /usage shows session per-model totals and sometimes credits without token counts; account views, authorized billing reports and Chronicle cost-tips answer different questions.
limitations: Chronicle analysis is not an invoice and may involve model work; organization-billed seats need organization reporting; billing REST is not detailed per-call trace.

claim: Claude Code /usage API session cost is an estimate and not subscription billing; reusable Claude instructions and skills are distinct from session transcripts.
limitations: The clients' usage displays differ; Claude transcript/memory import into Copilot is not established.

claim: Skill descriptions enable discovery, instructions load on invocation and supporting resources are available when needed in Copilot CLI.
limitations: Discovery does not prove invocation; review skill scripts/resources before using them.

claim: Copilot CLI @ prompt mentions attach the referenced file contents as context.
limitations: A plain path mention allows targeted discovery; do not assume @ is a deferred path lookup.

claim: The AI usage report breaks down model/user/token categories; REST billing report scope differs and SDK BYOK tracks provider usage, not GitHub Copilot usage.
limitations: Reports require authorized account access; no integration or billing experiment was run.

claim: Business/Enterprise included credits are pooled at the billing entity; paid completions and next-edit suggestions are not AI-credit billed, while hosted code review can involve credits and Actions minutes.
limitations: Personal consumption can be visible without a personal budget; hosted infrastructure accounting does not apply to ordinary local CLI review.

claim: CLI OpenTelemetry can expose operational model/tool activity and usage measurements.
limitations: Optional operational view, not the billing ledger; no exporter or content capture enabled.

claim: With limited permissions, Autopilot automatically denies tool requests that still require approval.
limitations: Use manual turns for per-write approval or previously reviewed grants; no authenticated permission behavior tested.

claim: GitHub's CLI engineering evaluations found that shortening tool output can increase total task work when missing evidence requires recovery; the post recommends evaluating completed tasks and preserving useful information.
limitations: Vendor advice and workload-specific experiments, not measured savings from this guide. June routing post describes VS Code implementation; CLI support requires separate evidence.
